subject.title: [Bug]: Slack replies ~2s slower than other channels — dominant cost is Socket Mode event delivery; channel-side stalls fixed in #101888

question: Should OpenClaw resolve this by documenting HTTP Request URLs as the preferred low-latency hosted Slack transport, or should Slack setup/default behavior change beyond the existing mode: "http" support?
rationale: HTTP mode already exists and the remaining measured delay is mostly before OpenClaw code runs, but steering or changing defaults affects Slack onboarding, public ingress requirements, and existing operator expectations.

options.title: Document HTTP latency guidance
options.body: Keep Socket Mode as the default for local/private deployments and explicitly recommend HTTP Request URLs for hosted public-ingress Slack deployments where reply latency matters.

options.title: Change setup or defaults
options.body: Have maintainers sponsor a stronger setup/default change that steers new hosted Slack installs away from Socket Mode, with upgrade and operator guidance.

options.title: Accept current guidance
options.body: Record that the current transport table is sufficient and close only after maintainers decide no additional latency-specific docs or setup change is planned.

recommendation.title: Document HTTP latency guidance
recommendation.body: Keep Socket Mode as the default for local/private deployments and explicitly recommend HTTP Request URLs for hosted public-ingress Slack deployments where reply latency matters.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the measurement, landed the partial Slack latency fix, and explicitly scoped the remaining follow-up to HTTP mode guidance.
